# Appendix C Deterministic and Two-Stage Stochastic MILP Implementations in Python and GAMS

## Mathematical implementation and terminology

The mathematical foundation is attributed to Rosa (2026). This appendix documents
the approved scalar implementation, not the archived hierarchical objective.
The scientific source inspected here is pinned at
[`6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4`](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/tree/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic).
The editorial additions do not modify that source. Source references identify
functions, not a claim that an old certificate was generated with the editorial
commit. Each accepted execution retains its own source and runtime identities.

Permanent implementation references are the
[Gurobi extensive-form builder](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic/optimization_gurobipy_stochastic.py#L40),
[native SCIP builder](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic/optimization_scip.py#L59),
[effective-input preparation](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic/mathematical_contract.py#L98),
[Excel loader](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic/excel_loader.py#L155)
and [independent residual/cost validator](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/6fb43389ea70b02d0f54c959a2bfff8d53d83af4/src/logic/solution_validation.py#L37).

We use Origin–Warehouse–Destination. In the Python records the Portuguese legacy
letter D denotes *depósito*, not the destination or the direct-enabled topology.
The crosswalk below prevents an ambiguity in reading the formulation and exports.
No serialized field or internal scientific identifier is renamed.

| Scientific transport family | Endpoints | Legacy code/artifact label | GAMS set / flow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OW | Origin → warehouse | OD | `ow / xOW` |
| WD | Warehouse → destination | DC | `wd / xWD` |
| WW | Warehouse → warehouse | DD | `ww / xWW` |
| OD, direct | Origin → destination | OC | `direct / xOD` |

W disables the last family; D permits it alongside all admissible warehouse
paths. D does not prescribe a positive direct flow. Both modes retain the same
three slack families and first-stage decisions. The accepted large scalar cohort
in this article contains W observations only. Software support for D is not a
controlled large-instance W×D result.

## Deterministic Python and Gurobi path

`optimization.solve_model` dispatches to
`optimization_gurobipy.solve_model_gurobipy`. This actual entry point uses
`mathematical_contract.extensive_form_inputs`, then
`optimization_gurobipy_stochastic.solve_stochastic_model_gurobipy`.
DET embeds the original deterministic supply and demand arrays in a singleton
named `deterministic`, with probability one. It neither averages stochastic
trajectories nor selects a convenient realization. `project_deterministic_result`
restores the deterministic output API after extraction.

The following excerpt is from the actual dispatcher, not pseudocode:

```python
prepared, config = extensive_form_inputs(data, model_config)
result = solve_stochastic_model_gurobipy(prepared, config, solver_config)
```

The common builder first freezes the selected graph and penalty vector, creates
the eligible first-stage binaries and quantities once, and creates nonnegative
flows only on retained product-specific arcs. Inventory is warehouse/product/
period indexed; shortage is domestic destination/product/period indexed; static
and reception slacks are separate warehouse/period variables. An absent arc is
not a zero-cost dense route. Explicit supply, initial stock and finite or
unrestricted export bounds retain their original interpretation.

## Stochastic Python and Gurobi path

STO shares candidate opening, candidate capacity, expansion and conversion
variables across scenarios by construction. Operating variables acquire a
scenario index. There are no scenario-specific investment copies to reconcile
after solving. Each realization supplies its full operating trajectory, so this
is a two-stage model despite its 60 periods, not a multistage policy.

The following actual objective-construction excerpt follows scenario cost
construction in `solve_stochastic_model_gurobipy`:

```python
expected_costs = {
    component: gp.quicksum(
        data.scenario_prob[scenario] * scenario_costs[scenario][component]
        for scenario in scenarios
    )
    for component in next(iter(scenario_costs.values()))
}
model.setObjective(penalized_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)
```

Investment is charged once; probabilities multiply transport, storage and each
slack cost once. They never scale conservation equations, installed capacity or
the shared investment vector. `_optimize_scalar` makes one native call; the
global TimeLimit does not restart at successive objective priorities.

## Python and SCIP path for DET and STO

`optimization_scip.solve_model_scip` uses the same deterministic embedding and
effective-input preparation. It reuses algebraic investment, capacity and unit-
cost helpers but creates native PySCIPOpt variables, constraints, indicators,
objective, solve call and result extraction. Shared helpers do not instantiate
a Gurobi environment. The SCIP extensive form creates separate scenario-indexed
operational records and one first-stage dictionary.

The source sets a single minimization of `penalized`, then calls
`model.optimize()`. SCIP's requested thread ceilings are not a claim that its
sequential optimize driver achieves concurrent search. Its native termination
and native gap remain distinct from the common incumbent-denominator gap.
The configured mathematical feasibility rules and original-unit independent
validator are not replaced by a solver's status label.

For inactive candidate slacks, Gurobi uses `addGenConstrIndicator` with binary
value false and equality zero. SCIP uses `addConsIndicator` with `activeone=False`
and a nonnegative slack bounded above by zero. These describe the same implication.
Neither translation requires inventing a finite upper bound on the active slack.
No SCIP/h215 large-instance success or failure under the current scalar contract
is inferred from these source correspondences or the analytical tests.

## Equation to code to data crosswalk

Equation identifiers refer to the complete main-text formulation. D3 defines
capacity expressions rather than additional optimization decisions.

| Equations / units | Actual Python function or construction | GAMS symbol/equation | Effective input origin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1, S1; BRL | `_build_investment_costs`, `_build_scenario_costs`; common builder objective | `objective`, `fixed*`, `unit*`, `cost*`, `hold`, `penalty*`, `pi` | Warehouse investment rules, freight × OSRM distances, tariffs and frozen weights; Appendix D |
| D2; investment t and binaries | `_add_first_stage_constraints` in stochastic Gurobi module; reused algebraically by SCIP | `newBound`, `expBound`, `bulkBound`, `expActive`, `bulkActive`, `exclusion` | Eligible subsets, maximum quantities and flags from `_load_warehouses` |
| D3; t and t/day | `_effective_static_capacity_expr`, `_effective_reception_capacity_expr`, `_effective_shipping_capacity_expr` | RHS of `stockBound`, `receiveBound`, `shipBound` | Initial capacities, day factors and investment-to-handling coefficients |
| D4/S2; period t | `_add_scenario_constraints` supply balance; native SCIP flow sums | `supplyBalance`, `supply` | Original supply or approved Cartesian multiplier |
| D5–D6/S3–S4; period t | `_add_scenario_constraints` inventory balance and explicit predecessor stock | `inventoryBalance`, `initial` | Retained OW/WD/WW arcs, initial inventory and ordered periods |
| D7/S5; period t | Domestic sum of DC + OC + shortage | `domesticBalance`, `demand` | Role-separated domestic data, scenario multiplier |
| D8/S6; period t | Export sum of DC + OC at most the upper bound | `exportBound`, `exportCap` | Declared fixed or supply-derived export limits |
| D9/S7; stock t, period handling t | Product-aggregated stock, inbound and outbound constraints | `stockBound`, `receiveBound`, `shipBound` | Daily rates × operating days; reception slack added afterward |
| D10/S8; slack t | Native candidate indicators in both backends | `closedStock`, `closedReception` plus mandatory solver mapping | Candidate membership and common opening binary |
| D11/S9; domains | Eligible first-stage keys, nonnegative recourse variables | `y,z,g,k,e,b,x*,stock,unmet,qK,qR` and subset fixes | ModelConfig and actual effective index sets |
| All residuals and D1/S1 cost | `solution_validation.validate_solution` | Independent comparison required; not supplied by `modelstat` alone | Frozen input plus sparse flow/stock/slack and dense first-stage exports |

The scalar cost has 14 independently reconstructed components: six investment,
four transport, one storage and three artificial penalties. The validator uses
absolute tolerance $10^{-5}$ and relative tolerance $10^{-8}$ locally for each
constraint, with the existing explicit sparse-export rounding budget. Aggregate
national balance cannot compensate for a failed local constraint.

## GAMS deterministic and stochastic translations

The reviewable source consists of `model_det.gms`, `model_sto.gms` and one shared
`model_common.inc`, distributed with this supplement. The two entry files
select the input interpretation; the common file contains the complete scalar
objective, all physical constraints, domains, eligibility and activation rows.
`scripts/export_scalar_gams_data.py` exports already effective Python inputs as
`data.inc` plus a JSON identifier/symbol/hash receipt. It does not build a solver
model, call GAMS, or change source spreadsheets. Safe synthetic GAMS labels map
back to every original node, product, period and scenario identifier. No manual
transcription of the large arrays is required.

The translation deliberately supports the accepted scalable-candidate,
daily-handling-factor, free-terminal, three-enabled-slack profile. Unsupported
legacy settings fail rather than being approximately translated. The exporter
preserves original DET data, probabilities, route filtering, all unit costs,
initial stocks, eligible investment bounds and the effective penalty vector.
The file hash identifies its generated bytes; the receipt additionally binds
the workbook, manifest, case and source. Parameter exports remain local if their
redistribution conditions are not established.

GAMS passes indicator mappings through solver-specific option files, rather than
ordinary endogenous dollar conditions. The common file writes the mandatory
Gurobi mapping or SCIP indicator-file reference. Omitting that mapping would
solve a different model. The mechanism follows the
[GAMS indicator documentation](https://www.gams.com/latest/docs/UG_LanguageFeatures.html#UG_LanguageFeatures_IndicatorConstraints)
and [GAMS/SCIP interface](https://www.gams.com/latest/docs/S_SCIP.html).
No arbitrary slack Big-M is introduced. Default execution performs source/data
inspection without a solve. An explicit tiny-local flag is restricted by size;
full h215/h300/h400/h500 numerical reproduction is not admitted here.

## Structural and numerical validation status

**C1, structural inspection:** the crosswalk, shared first-stage indexing,
probability placement, four flow families, capacity units, three slacks and
native-indicator mapping were inspected against the pinned Python source.
Exporter tests check original input preservation, costs, scenarios, configuration
rejection and exclusive output. This is not a GAMS compiler certificate.

**C2, small numerical parity:** unperformed. No GAMS executable is installed in
the qualification environment; GAMS compilation, solver loading and numerical
parity are not claimed. Existing Python Gurobi/SCIP analytical tests concern
those backends, not execution of this translation. A future licensed small test
must compare objective components, residuals and meaningful decisions, allowing
alternative optima rather than demanding identical arbitrary binary choices.

**C3, full-instance reproduction:** unperformed and not authorized. Accepted
Python h215/h300/h400 records remain the empirical evidence; they do not validate
GAMS by proxy. Full translation runs would require input review, appropriate
licenses, resources, explicit scientific authorization and their own immutable
certificates. Publication or production deployment is not implied.
